summary: The narrator confronts a DHS agent who held her in a hospital room after airlifting her there, and refuses to be controlled. Holding the agent's gun, she leaves the building in a borrowed hospital gown's place with her own clothes, steals a car, and drives into the Southern California desert. There she stops, aches from a wound in her side, a popped-back broken thumb, and a burned left hand, and pulls out a pocket multitool, preparing to remove the tracker implanted in her side.
one_line: A wounded narrator escapes a DHS agent's hospital room, steals a car, and flees into the California desert with a multitool, intent on cutting out a tracker.
key_facts: The narrator tells the DHS agent that she has been left unsecured after being airlifted to the nearest hospital.
The narrator suspects the agent did not move her to a secure location because she wanted to keep a leash on her.
The narrator threatens the agent: "Get out of my way," I said. "Or so help me, I will shoot you."
The agent straightens and moves aside, and the narrator edges out of the room while keeping the agent's own gun on her.
The narrator's broken thumb twinged when she scooped up her clothes with the hand not holding the gun.
The narrator changed clothes in a stairwell and walked out of the hospital into bright sunlight with no other security.
The DHS left the contents of the narrator's pockets untouched, but her shirt was missing, probably cut off by a surgeon.
The narrator zipped up her jacket to hide the missing shirt, despite the Southern California warmth.
The narrator steals the first car she comes to and drives out past the outskirts of LA into the desert.
The narrator pulls the car off the road into empty desert and stops, with the sun beating through the windshield.
She popped her broken thumb back into place on her way out of the hospital, but it still sends spasms up her right arm.
The burn on her left hand, under the dressing, has started to prickle again.
She had dropped her main knife in the diner when she was taken, but still had a pocket multitool with a blade.
The narrator describes the tracker in her side as releasing a toxic poison and taking her over, making her theirs.
